title: Terms of Registration for Medical and Life-Support Protections: Withdrawal, Moving and Closing Service
content:
These terms apply to every protection registered under Medical and Life-Support Protections.

**(a) Withdrawal.** The customer may withdraw a protection at any time, and must report when the patient no longer lives at the address. Withdrawal is the customer's own act and ends the protections as the protection's withdrawal terms provide. On withdrawal the registration moves from active to withdrawn, with the withdrawal date recorded.

**(b) Moving.** When the customer moves, a protection whose certification moves with the patient to the customer's new service agreement is registered on the new service agreement from the same certification for the rest of its term, and the old registration is withdrawn. Other protections end with the old agreement.

**(c) Closing service.** When the service agreement closes, its protections are withdrawn on the stop date.

## The terms set out by situation

| Situation | Who acts | Result |
|---|---|---|
| The customer no longer wants the protection | the customer, by withdrawing | the registration is withdrawn; the protections end as the withdrawal terms provide |
| The patient no longer lives at the address | the customer must report it | the registration is withdrawn |
| The customer moves, protection transferable to the new agreement | — | registered on the new service agreement from the same certification for the rest of its term; the old registration withdrawn |
| The customer moves, protection not transferable | — | the protection ends with the old agreement |
| The service agreement closes | — | its protections are withdrawn on the stop date |

## Explanatory notes

- **The same certification.** A protection carried to the new service agreement keeps the certification it had: its certified date and its expiration date do not change, and it runs only for the rest of that term.
- **Any time.** Withdrawal is not tied to a notice period or to the end of the certification term.

*Hypothetical example:* a customer holding a Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance certified on 1 February, with the expiration date 31 January of the following year, moves on 15 August to a new address where the patient will live. The protection is registered on the new service agreement from the same certification and runs there until 31 January; the registration at the old address is withdrawn.
